design_notes: Pass 1 topics locked. Concept expansion covers all official-scope skill families: known-solid qualitative chemistry, polymer/fiber/hair microscopy, separations and spectra, fingerprints, DNA/blood, physical pattern reconstruction, field trace evidence, cross-cutting lab methods, and suspect reasoning. Concept counts vary from 8 to 14 based on real skill density; no topic left thin.

concepts.title: Solubility of the 15 listed solids in water
concepts.description: Classify each listed solid as soluble, slightly soluble, or insoluble in water at room temperature and use solubility as a first-step identification clue.

concepts.title: Solution pH and conductivity of solids
concepts.description: Dissolve known solids in water and use pH paper or universal indicator and conductivity to classify acidic, basic, or neutral salt solutions.

concepts.title: Flame test colors for listed metal salts
concepts.description: Identify sodium, potassium, lithium, calcium, magnesium, and boron species by the characteristic color each imparts to a clean flame.

concepts.title: Chloride test with silver nitrate
concepts.description: Add silver nitrate to a chloride-containing solution and interpret white AgCl precipitate that darkens in light as a positive chloride result.

concepts.title: Sulfate test with barium nitrate
concepts.description: Treat sulfate-containing samples with barium nitrate and interpret white BaSO4 precipitate insoluble in dilute acid as a positive sulfate test.

concepts.title: Carbonate and bicarbonate acid reaction test
concepts.description: Add dilute acid to carbonate or bicarbonate solids and recognize immediate effervescence of CO2 to distinguish them from non-carbonate solids.

concepts.title: Iodine test for starch
concepts.description: Use iodine solution to detect cornstarch by the blue-black starch-iodine complex and distinguish starch from glucose and sucrose.

concepts.title: Benedict's test for reducing sugars
concepts.description: Heat sample with Benedict's reagent and interpret brick-red Cu2O precipitate as positive for reducing sugars such as glucose.

concepts.title: Distinguishing sucrose from glucose
concepts.description: Perform Benedict's test before and after acid hydrolysis to identify sucrose, negative before and positive after, versus glucose, positive before.

concepts.title: Ammonium ion test with sodium hydroxide
concepts.description: Warm sample with NaOH and detect ammonia gas by odor or red litmus turning blue as a positive test for NH4Cl.

concepts.title: Acetate detection by acid odor
concepts.description: Add dilute sulfuric acid to sodium acetate and recognize vinegar-like acetic acid odor as a positive acetate test.

concepts.title: Nitrate test by brown ring
concepts.description: Layer iron(II) sulfate with concentrated sulfuric acid on sample solution and observe a brown ring at the interface as positive nitrate.

concepts.title: Boric acid identification
concepts.description: Identify boric acid by its green flame color, weak acid behavior, and greater solubility in hot water than in cold water.

concepts.title: Physical appearance and crystalline form of listed solids
concepts.description: Use crystal size, powder texture, color, and hygroscopic or deliquescent behavior as preliminary distinguishing observations among the 15 listed solids.

concepts.title: Polymer density separation by flotation
concepts.description: Use water, saturated salt, alcohol, and oil to separate common plastics by density ranges and identify PETE, HDPE, PS, LDPE, PP, PVC, PMMA, and PC.

concepts.title: Polymer flame test observations
concepts.description: Ignite small polymer samples and interpret flame color, smoke, dripping, self-extinguishing behavior, and odor to distinguish plastics.

concepts.title: Resin codes and physical properties of plastics
concepts.description: Correlate SPI resin codes 1-7 with polymer names and use clarity, flexibility, and hardness to distinguish PETE, HDPE, PVC, LDPE, PP, PS, and PC.

concepts.title: Chemical spot tests for polymers
concepts.description: Use specific chemical tests such as copper wire flame, acetone solubility, and alcohol flame to identify PVC, PMMA, PS, and other plastics.

concepts.title: Microscopic identification of natural fibers
concepts.description: Use microscope morphology including flat twists in cotton, nodes in linen, scales on wool, and smooth transparent tubes in silk to identify natural fibers.

concepts.title: Synthetic fiber burn and melt identification
concepts.description: Ignite fibers and use melting, bead formation, ash, odor, and smoke to distinguish nylon, polyester, and spandex.

concepts.title: Medulla patterns and human vs animal hair
concepts.description: Compare medullary index, pattern type, and pigment distribution to distinguish human hair from animal hair.

concepts.title: Cuticle scale patterns in hair
concepts.description: Recognize coronal, spinous, and imbricate cuticle scale patterns from casts or microscopy for species identification.

concepts.title: Hair root morphology and growth phase
concepts.description: Distinguish anagen, catagen, and telogen root appearance and use tissue tags or follicle shape to infer forcible removal or natural shedding.

concepts.title: Species identification from hair samples
concepts.description: Combine medulla type, cuticle scale pattern, color banding, and diameter to identify human, bat, cow, squirrel, and horse hair.

concepts.title: Paper chromatography separation principle
concepts.description: Explain how analytes partition between a polar stationary phase and a mobile solvent and predict migration based on polarity and intermolecular forces.

concepts.title: Thin-layer chromatography principle
concepts.description: Describe TLC separation on silica or alumina plates, compare with paper, and use UV visualization or staining to locate analyte spots.

concepts.title: Rf calculation and interpretation
concepts.description: Calculate retention factor as distance moved by compound divided by distance moved by solvent front and use Rf to compare unknowns with standards.

concepts.title: Chromatogram development and sample application
concepts.description: Prepare a chromatogram by spotting small concentrated samples, suspending the plate or paper without submerging the spot, and developing in a sealed chamber.

concepts.title: Visualization of chromatograms
concepts.description: Choose appropriate visualization methods such as UV lamp, iodine vapor, ninhydrin, or visible dyes to reveal separated colorless analytes.

concepts.title: Molecular ion and molar mass from mass spectra
concepts.description: Identify the molecular ion peak to determine molar mass and distinguish M+ from fragment peaks and recognize M+1 and M+2 isotopic peaks.

concepts.title: Fragmentation patterns in mass spectra
concepts.description: Interpret major fragment peaks as losses of stable groups and use base peak and relative abundance to recognize structural subunits.

concepts.title: Isotope patterns for chlorine and bromine
concepts.description: Recognize characteristic M:M+2 intensity ratios for compounds containing chlorine about 3:1 or bromine about 1:1 from mass spectra.

concepts.title: Comparing chromatograms and mass spectra
concepts.description: Distinguish retention-based separation output from mass-to-charge spectral output and use both to identify forensic samples.

concepts.title: Friction ridge skin anatomy
concepts.description: Explain how friction ridges form from dermal papillae into the epidermis and how sweat and oil secretions create latent prints.

concepts.title: Arch fingerprint patterns
concepts.description: Identify and distinguish plain arches and tented arches by ridge flow across the finger and central spike or loop features.

concepts.title: Loop fingerprint patterns
concepts.description: Classify ulnar and radial loops by delta, core, and loop opening direction relative to the hand bones.

concepts.title: Whorl fingerprint patterns
concepts.description: Distinguish plain whorl, central pocket loop, double loop, and accidental whorl using number and placement of deltas and ridge structure.

concepts.title: Fingerprint minutiae identification
concepts.description: Recognize ending ridges, bifurcations, dots, lakes, spurs, and crossovers in a print and use their positions for individualization.

concepts.title: Powder development of latent prints
concepts.description: Apply fine fingerprint powder with a brush to nonporous surfaces and lift using tape and backing cards to develop and preserve latent prints.

concepts.title: Chemical development of latent prints
concepts.description: Choose and explain chemical methods including iodine fuming, ninhydrin, silver nitrate, and cyanoacrylate for porous and nonporous surfaces.

concepts.title: Cyanoacrylate fuming for latent prints
concepts.description: Describe superglue fuming chamber reactions with moisture and amino acids to form white polymerized ridges on nonporous evidence and use fluorescent dye staining for enhancement.

concepts.title: Types of fingerprints: latent, patent, plastic
concepts.description: Classify prints as latent, patent, or plastic and predict the optimal development method for each surface and print type.

concepts.title: ACE-V fingerprint comparison method
concepts.description: Apply Analysis, Comparison, Evaluation, and Verification stages to individualize or identify fingerprints and explain the basis for conclusions.

concepts.title: STR DNA profiling
concepts.description: Explain how short tandem repeat loci are counted by repeat number and how allele peaks on electropherograms identify a DNA profile.

concepts.title: DNA electropherogram peak interpretation
concepts.description: Read dye-labeled allele peaks, distinguish stutter and pull-up artifacts, and match allele sizes using size-standard ladders.

concepts.title: PCR amplification of DNA
concepts.description: Explain denaturation, annealing, and extension temperature cycling and how exponential amplification copies target STR regions from trace DNA.

concepts.title: DNA extraction and quantification
concepts.description: Lyse cells, purify DNA from proteins and inhibitors, and quantify DNA yield or concentration using UV absorbance or fluorometry before amplification.

concepts.title: ABO blood typing with antisera
concepts.description: Add anti-A, anti-B, and anti-D antisera to blood and interpret agglutination patterns to determine ABO and Rh type.

concepts.title: Blood cell microscopy and species identification
concepts.description: Use microscope slides to distinguish human blood cells from avian, mammalian, and reptile or amphibian blood by RBC shape, nucleation, and size.

concepts.title: Presumptive vs confirmatory blood tests
concepts.description: Choose Kastle-Meyer, luminol, or leucomalachite green as presumptive and Takayama or immunological tests as confirmatory and interpret controls.

concepts.title: DNA sequencing chromatogram reading
concepts.description: Read Sanger sequence chromatograms by colored dye peaks and quality scores and distinguish heterozygous peaks from background noise.

concepts.title: DNA mixture and contamination interpretation
concepts.description: Recognize mixed DNA profiles with more than two alleles at loci, interpret major and minor contributors, and identify possible contamination or allelic dropout.

concepts.title: ABO inheritance and prediction
concepts.description: Use ABO genotypes IA, IB, and i to predict possible offspring blood types and evaluate whether a suspect could be a source.

topics.title: Glass fracture, bloodstain pattern, and bullet striation analysis

concepts.title: Glass refractive index by immersion
concepts.description: Use the Becke line method with immersion oils of known refractive index to determine glass refractive index and compare questioned and known glass.

concepts.title: Glass density flotation comparison
concepts.description: Compare glass density by sink or float in liquids of known density to determine if fragments originate from the same source.

concepts.title: Radial and concentric glass fractures
concepts.description: Distinguish radial cracks from concentric circles and use their orientation and morphology to identify impact side and direction.

concepts.title: Determining glass fracture order
concepts.description: Apply fracture termination rules where cracks stop at existing fractures to sequence multiple bullet or impact hits in glass.

concepts.title: Bloodstain angle of impact calculation
concepts.description: Measure stain width and length and calculate angle of impact using sin θ = width/length to reconstruct drop direction.

concepts.title: Bloodstain velocity and size classification
concepts.description: Relate droplet size and misting to low, medium, or high velocity impact mechanisms such as gravity, cast-off, or gunshot.

concepts.title: Bloodstain point of origin reconstruction
concepts.description: Use multiple stain angle and direction lines via strings or trigonometric tangent to locate the area of origin in three dimensions.

concepts.title: Bullet lands and grooves striations
concepts.description: Explain rifling marks on bullets including lands and grooves and compare individual striations on test-fired bullets under a comparison microscope.

concepts.title: Bullet and cartridge class characteristics
concepts.description: Use caliber, number, width, and direction of lands and grooves, and cartridge case markings to classify ammunition and narrow weapon type.

topics.title: Entomology, palynology, soil, and track evidence

concepts.title: Blow fly life cycle and PMI
concepts.description: Estimate postmortem interval using developmental stages of blow fly eggs, larval instars, prepupae, pupae, and adults at known temperatures.

concepts.title: Accumulated degree day/hour calculation for PMI
concepts.description: Calculate PMI from insect development using species-specific thermal requirements and accumulated degree days or hours.

concepts.title: Insect succession on carrion
concepts.description: Use predictable waves of insect colonization and environmental conditions to estimate decomposition stage and PMI range.

concepts.title: Pollen and spore identification
concepts.description: Use size, shape, aperture type, and surface ornamentation under light or SEM microscopy to identify pollen and spore taxa and infer location or season.

concepts.title: Soil color, texture, and particle composition
concepts.description: Characterize soil by Munsell color, grain size distribution of sand, silt, and clay, and organic or mineral content for source comparison.

concepts.title: Soil chemical and mineral tests
concepts.description: Test soil pH, effervescence with acid, and presence of minerals such as quartz using simple chemical or optical tests to link soil samples.

concepts.title: Track measurement and gait analysis
concepts.description: Measure stride length, track depth, straddle, and foot or paw size to infer height, speed, load, and number of individuals.

concepts.title: Shoe and tire impression comparison
concepts.description: Compare class and wear or defect characteristics in shoe and tire impressions to include or exclude footwear or vehicles as evidence sources.

concepts.title: Casting and lifting impression evidence
concepts.description: Choose dental stone or plaster for 3D impressions and electrostatic or gelatin lifters for 2D dust impressions and document and preserve impressions.

topics.title: Forensic lab methods and data handling

concepts.title: Use of controls, blanks, and standards
concepts.description: Include positive and negative controls, reagent blanks, and known standards in every test to validate results and detect contamination.

concepts.title: Measurement precision and significant figures
concepts.description: Record measurements with correct precision and significant figures and use balances, graduated cylinders, rulers, and micropipettes to match instrument uncertainty.

concepts.title: Microscope setup and use in forensics
concepts.description: Set up compound and stereomicroscopes, choose magnification, focus, adjust field and condenser, and record measurements from calibrated eyepiece or camera.

concepts.title: Sample preparation for forensic tests
concepts.description: Prepare solid or liquid samples by cutting, scraping, dissolving, filtering, centrifuging, or diluting without altering evidence and preserve representative portions.

concepts.title: Laboratory safety and personal protection
concepts.description: Apply PPE, fume hood use, chemical hygiene, eye and skin wash, and safe handling and disposal of biological and chemical evidence in forensic labs.

concepts.title: Documentation and chain of custody
concepts.description: Maintain labeled evidence seals, log transfer dates and signatures, and record observations with initials and dates to preserve admissibility and continuity.

concepts.title: Data recording and result calculations
concepts.description: Organize qualitative observations and quantitative measurements into tables and calculate concentrations, dilutions, densities, and angle measurements with correct units.

concepts.title: Instrument calibration and verification
concepts.description: Calibrate balances, pH meters, thermocyclers, and micropipettes using known standards and verify calibration before and after evidence measurements.

concepts.title: Avoiding cross-contamination
concepts.description: Use sterile or disposable tools, change gloves between items, separate evidence samples, and clean surfaces to prevent evidence contamination and false associations.

concepts.title: Error sources and uncertainty in forensic measurements
concepts.description: Identify random and systematic errors, estimate uncertainty, and evaluate false positives and negatives in qualitative and quantitative forensic tests.

topics.title: Crime scene analysis and suspect reasoning

concepts.title: Class vs individual evidence
concepts.description: Distinguish class characteristics such as fiber type or blood group from individualizing characteristics such as fingerprint minutiae, DNA profiles, or bullet striations and assess probative value.

concepts.title: Inculpatory vs exculpatory evidence
concepts.description: Classify evidence as inculpatory, supporting involvement, or exculpatory, tending to exclude a suspect, and use both to test hypotheses.

concepts.title: Suspect implication and elimination logic
concepts.description: Write reasoning that compares suspect reference samples to evidence, stating matches, mismatches, and whether evidence implicates or eliminates each suspect.

concepts.title: Integrating multiple evidence types
concepts.description: Combine results from different evidence categories such as DNA, fiber, and fingerprints into a coherent scenario and evaluate corroboration and contradictions.

concepts.title: Evaluating evidence admissibility and chain of custody defects
concepts.description: Assess whether breaks in chain of custody, mislabeling, or improper storage compromise evidence integrity and affect admissibility in suspect reasoning.

concepts.title: Reliability and limitations of forensic tests
concepts.description: Assess sensitivity, specificity, false positive and negative rates, and interpretation limits for each forensic test before drawing suspect conclusions.

concepts.title: Scenario reconstruction and hypothesis testing
concepts.description: Use evidence patterns such as spatter, glass, and tracks to reconstruct the sequence of events and test alternative hypotheses for consistency.

concepts.title: Writing forensic conclusion reasoning
concepts.description: Construct clear evidence-based conclusions using claim-evidence-reasoning format with specific test results and logical justification for each suspect.
